title: Casper and the Orchard
premise: In 1934, on a fog-bound island off the northern coast, widowed lighthouse keeper Vesper Zhou keeps his lamp lit and his grief private. When the seasonal bridge closes and the island's magistrate begins seizing the fishing families' deeds under cover of the great storms, Vesper is handed a ledger proving the fraud — by a dying clerk named Casper, whose name the islanders give to the stray orchard tree outside the lighthouse. Smuggling the ledger past three checkpoints before the magistrate's men burn the records, Vesper loses the lamp, nearly loses his daughter, and learns that belonging is something you carry, not something you're given. The book ends with the magistrate's fall in spring, Vesper planting the orchard's seedlings on the mainland shore, and the light — kept by the community now — burning without him.
about_author: Ivo Oyelaran is a former archivist who grew up between a fishing village and a port city, and writes about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.' Casper and the Orchard is his second novel, inspired by a box of unclaimed land deeds he once catalogued.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Lamp
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. We meet him winding the lighthouse clockwork, measuring his life in portable things — a habit from his late wife's illness. Emotional beat: quiet grief and rigid order, established before anything breaks it.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The bridge closes for the season; the ferryman warns that Magistrate Corren has been buying debts cheap. Vesper's daughter Nell befriends a stray dog at the orchard tree. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Clerk in the Dunes
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The magistrate's clerk, Casper, copies fraudulent seizure orders by lamplight, sick with what he's complicit in. He pockets one true ledger. Beat: conscience waking.

chapters.title: Storm Signs
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell watches the fishing families barter their boats against debts they can't see. She names the orchard tree 'Casper' for no reason she can explain. Beat: childhood clarity cutting through adult evasion.

chapters.title: The First Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Bringing oil from the mainland store, Vesper is stopped at the bridge checkpoint and sees Corren's men logging every departure. Beat: the island becoming a cage.

chapters.title: Casper at the Door
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Wounded and feverish, Casper reaches the lighthouse and gives Vesper the ledger — proof Corren manufactured the debts. Beat: a dying man's desperate trust.

chapters.title: What the Dead Ask
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper buries Casper beneath the orchard and argues with himself all night: hand the ledger to Corren and be safe, or carry it out. Beat: the cost of choosing.

chapters.title: The Widow Osei's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Widow Osei's POV. The island's matriarch reads the ledger and organizes quietly — who can hide Vesper, who can forge a pass. Beat: community as conspiracy of care.

chapters.title: Corren Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. The magistrate visits the lighthouse, charming and menacing, offering Vesper a mainland posting in exchange for 'any papers the clerk may have left.' Beat: power's velvet glove.

chapters.title: Nell's Secret
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell has already found the ledger's hiding place — inside Casper's grave marker — and tells a schoolmate, who tells her brother, who works for Corren. Beat: innocence with consequences.

chapters.title: The Great Storm Arrives
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The first of the great storms batters the island; the light must be kept or ships die. Vesper keeps it while soldiers search his home below. Beat: duty and danger in one body.

chapters.title: Burn the Records
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, posthumous — his journal, found by Osei. It reveals a second copy of the ledger hidden in the customs house, and that Corren plans to burn everything at season's end. Beat: stakes made explicit.

chapters.title: The Second Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Disguised as an oil courier, Vesper moves the ledger toward the customs house through the flooded causeway, nearly drowning. Beat: survival at physical cost.

chapters.title: A Traitor's Bargain
chapters.summary: Osei's POV. The schoolmate's brother betrays the plan to save his own family's deed; Osei must decide whether to silence or forgive him. Beat: the corruption survival demands.

chapters.title: The Customs House Fire
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper reaches the second ledger as Corren's men set the fire; he saves the pages but his hands are burned and his face is now known. Beat: triumph that exposes him.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Corren takes Nell as 'a guest of the magistrate' until her father surrenders the papers. Beat: the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: The Third Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. To trade himself for Nell, Vesper must pass the bridge checkpoint with both ledgers sewn into his coat — and the ferryman, once a coward, chooses to help. Beat: redemption in small hands.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. The exchange on the storm-lashed pier; Corren takes the ledgers, believing them complete — but Osei's forger has salted them, and the true pages ride with Nell's dog. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: The Light Goes Out
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Imprisoned in the lighthouse, Vesper watches Corren's men extinguish the lamp — a ship founders on the rocks, and the island sees exactly what Corren's rule costs. Beat: catastrophe as revelation.

chapters.title: The Island Rises
chapters.summary: Osei's POV. With the true ledger, the fishing families and the mainland inspector Corren feared confront him at the bridge; the islanders, armed with nothing but testimony and numbers, take the checkpoint. Beat: collective courage, the climax.

chapters.title: Spring Crossing
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The bridge opens; Corren is carried off to trial, the deeds returned. Vesper, hands still bandaged, digs up Casper's seedlings. Beat: grief turning toward growth.

chapters.title: The Orchard on the Mainland Shore
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. The community keeps the lighthouse now, rotating keepers; Vesper and Nell plant the orchard across the water, where they can see the light at night. Beat: belonging carried, not granted — resolution.
